key_insight: Task-specific quality gating for OCT choroid segmentation works better with learned image representations than with hand-crafted no-reference quality scores, especially when using retinal foundation models.
clinical_relevance: More reliable scan filtering could help automated retinal image analysis avoid bad-segmentation failures and improve consistency in biomarker extraction workflows.
method: Evaluated 6,076 OCT B-scans from 80 subjects for task-specific quality gating
Compared scalar NR-IQA metrics with supervised linear probing and unsupervised K-Means on pretrained representations
Benchmarked general-purpose ImageNet models and retinal foundation models against a patient-level null
evidence_signal: All scalar metrics were weak (|r| < 0.20), while learned embeddings improved ROC-AUC up to 0.77 and RETFound reached about 0.81, with retinal foundation models also forming quality-aligned clusters above a permutation null.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated for one prototype task (choroid segmentation) on a specific dataset, so broader generalization and deployment thresholds still need external validation.
paper_title: Task-Specific Quality Gating for Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans: Learned Representations Over Scalar Metrics in Choroid Segmentation
